newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach to run trains on Isle of Wight.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach to run trains on Isle of Wight.

text.p: British bus and train operator Stagecoach Holdings Plc won its second UK passenger rail company franchise on Friday when it was confirmed as the new private operator of the Island Line on England's Isle of Wight.
Island Line, only 8.5 miles (12 km) long and with three stations, serves local residents and tourists.

A statement from the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) said Stagecoach would run the line for an initial five years and receive a subsidy of just over 2.0 million stg in the first year, falling to 1.75 million stg in year five.
As part of its operating contract, Stagecoach has agreed to introduce a local resident's travel scheme and try out other discounted fares.
The line will continue to be operated by British Rail until completion of legal and safety requirements.
Last December Stagecoach became the first private firm to take over a full passenger service when it was awarded the franchise to run regional commuter line South West Trains.
